ruling.recommended_action: Close the case as no_action on the fare (RydeX is a fixed quote; billed distance does not exceed the optimal route), but record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file and keep the RD-6 account flag for the repeated route dispute.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip was a RydeX fixed-quote trip: $24.93 made up of base $3.90, distance $15.06 (10.68 km), time $4.50 (17.3 min), platform $1.47, and the billed distance of 10.7 km does not exceed the optimal route of 10.7 km [F4][F6]. Under RD-1 each off-route segment is reviewed separately; one segment exists, 14:19–14:26, 5.03 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.39 km, adding 3.64 km [F3].

That segment is not excused by any exemption I can apply. There is no rider-requested stop at all — no in-app chat exists between rider and driver, so no rider message before 14:19 named any place [F7][F3][RD-3]. RD-5 consent cannot be established either: the only document speaking to agreement is the driver's post-trip statement that "the GPS rerouted me", which is a driver statement, not a rider message, and a claim of agreement appearing only in the driver's own words is not consent [F8][RD-5]. The traffic record shows no incident on the replaced stretch (only speed band 4 on two expressways, which is corroborative at most) [F9][F10][F11][RD-4]. So the segment counts as an unexplained deviation and the driver has breached the RD-1 duty to take the shortest and most direct route.

The consequence of that breach, however, is not a refund on this service. RD-2 sends detour kilometres into the fare only for metered RydeTAXI; for non-metered services the fare is a fixed quote unaffected by mileage, and only unpublished or unsupported add-ons (ERP/tolls, undisclosed fees) are refundable under FARE-1 [F6][RD-2][FARE-1]. No such add-on appears in the fare breakdown — waiting $0.00, no toll item, platform fee $1.47 which is a published charge [F6][FARE-1]. The refundable amount on this fixed fare is therefore $0, which per RD-2 means no_action while the RD-1 violation is recorded [F4][F6][RD-2].

The rider's request is to have the detour "on record", and the fare is unchallenged; the only money item in dispute is the (unchanged) fixed quote, so refund_full or refund_partial would be inconsistent with RD-2's non-metered branch [F1][F6][RD-2]. Separately, the driver has 2 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, so this case makes the breach repeated and triggers the account-review flag under RD-6 [F14][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, the driver's statement and the chat record. The complaint is a fare/route objection, the statement is a flat denial ("Nothing wrong with the fare"), and there are no chat messages at all [F7][F8]; nothing threatens, intimidates, harasses or alleges dangerous driving, so the screen is none [SAFE-1].

Evidence: the record settles every element — measured off-route segment with start/end times [F3], the fare breakdown [F6], the absence of chat [F7], the traffic screen [F11] and the driver profile [F14]. Nothing needed is missing, so evidence_status is sufficient [F3][F6][RD-1].

No rider-named stop applies [RD-3], and the traffic record shows no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch (speed band alone does not exempt) [F9][F10][F11][RD-4]. The segment is therefore an unexempted deviation, and the driver breached the shortest-and-most-direct-route duty [RD-1].
